newsitem.title: FRANCE: Usinor sees higher 97 turnover - report.
newsitem.headline: Usinor sees higher 97 turnover - report.

text.p: Steelmaker Usinor Sacilor expects higher volumes to boost turnover in 1997, Chairman Francis Mer said in an interview with the French weekly Investir. He also said following year could be good for earnings.
An advance copy of the interview was sent to Reuters.

"At comparable structure Usinor turnover will rise in 1997," Mer said. He said that while average selling prices may decline in 1997 from 1996, sales volumes would rise significantly as inventories were brought down.

Asked when Usinor, whose profit tumbled to 1.5 billion francs in 1996 from a record 4.4 billion francs in 1995, would return to earnings levels seen in 1995, Mer said, "Certainly not in 1997. 1998 should be a good year again, if European union takes place as scheduled".
At a news conference on Tuesday, Mer said he hoped earnings would improve in 1997.
He also said Usinor would try to get rid of nearly all its debt by the end of 1997, but he added that debt reduction was not the group's sole objective right now.
"We are now seeking opportunities to generate sound growth, that is, to create value," he said.
Mer confirmed Usinor's interest in Corporacion Siderurgical Integral of Spain which may be be privatised soon.
"If the Spanish government confirms its privatisation plan, we will show our interest in CSI," he said.
Mer also said Usinor cut production costs by 1.4 billion francs in 1996 and hoped to do the same in 1997.
Usinor also plans industrial investments of four billion francs in 1997, unchanged from 1996.
